title: Responses compatibility fidelity mapping & staged test harness
creator: Lina Chen
description: Inventory and map behavioral differences between Redwood Responses implementation and upstream OpenAI Responses API across streaming, tool/function calling, and structured output semantics. Deliver a staged, automated test harness + golden prompt corpus that quantifies fidelity gaps and provides pragmatic adapter strategies (strict mapping, best-effort mapping, and opt-in behavioral compatibility flags).
acceptance_criteria: Catalog of functional deltas covering streaming events, partial tokens, finalization events, tool/function call shapes, and structured output field names produced and validated for 120 representative prompts.
Automated test harness that can run against runtime-2.4 candidate and an OpenAI Responses reference implementation to compute mismatch metrics (event-level, token-level, and semantic output-level).
Compatibility mapping RFC with three adapter modes (strict, permissive, and shim) and recommended default mode for hosted vs dedicated customers.
Canary plan defined with traffic split, health checks, rollback triggers, and monitoring dashboards wired to Redwood Console alerts.
tasks: Assemble golden prompt corpus (streaming, tool calls, structured output, edge cases like generator stops/partial tool calls).
Implement reference harness runner that records and normalizes event streams from both Redwood runtime and OpenAI Responses mock.
Define normalization rules for token diffs, metadata fields (e.g., 'tool_calls' vs 'function_call'), and streaming delta frames.
Prototype three adapter strategies: strict adapter (fail on mismatch), best-effort adapter (map or synthesize fields), and shim layer that translates event envelopes.
Add unit and integration tests for tool-call handoff (tool selection, args typing, multiple tool call streaming), including failure/retry scenarios.
Create canary orchestration: route 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% with automatic rollback on mismatch_rate > 0.5% or p95 latency spike > 2x baseline.
Prepare docs and SDK snippet changes for openai-responses compatibility guide and migration checklist.
test_plan: Unit tests for consumer-facing event shapes (on_delta, on_tool_call, on_done) including out-of-order delta delivery simulation.
Integration tests comparing full session traces between Redwood runtime and OpenAI reference; compute: token_alignment_rate, event_order_mismatch_rate, semantic_diff_score.
Fuzzing harness that mutates stop sequences, tool arg serializations, and streaming chunk boundaries to surface brittle mapping rules.
Golden verification: 120 prompts executed against both systems nightly; generate daily delta report and attach to ticket.
Customer scenario smoke tests: webhook-based tool-call flows, function-call fallbacks, and structured JSON-LD outputs validated against schema.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): run harness against runtime-2.4 branch in CI; fix immediate mapping bugs.
Stage 1 (canary): route 1% of hosted API traffic for customers opted into 'compat-mode=beta'; monitor mismatch metrics and user errors.
Stage 2 (ramp): increase to 25% with selective dedicated pools for higher fidelity checks; run manual QA on top customer prompts.
Stage 3 (ga opt-in): enable permissive shim by default for new accounts; document opt-out path and strict mode for customers needing exact parity.
Rollback: automatic based on alert thresholds; postmortem and hotfix flow documented.
metrics: event_level_mismatch_rate: percentage of response events that differ in type or ordering between Redwood and reference.
token_alignment_rate: fraction of tokens aligned after normalization (ignores whitespace/encoding differences).
semantic_diff_score: normalized embedding cosine distance between final outputs (accept threshold >= 0.95 similarity).
tool_call_fidelity: percentage of tool invocations where name+args+timing match expected reference.
p95_latency_change: compare 7d baseline to canary; rollback if >2x for production customers.
decisions: Normalization layer will canonicalize streaming delta frames by aggregating consecutive small deltas into logical tokens when safe—reduces false-positive mismatch noise.
Default adapter mode for hosted API will be 'best-effort' to avoid breaking most integrations; strict mode available behind flag and for Dedicated/Private customers.
Tool-calling mapping will prioritize preservation of 'name' + structured args; if exact schema mismatch, adapter will emit a compatibility wrapper and log a deprecation warning.
